marina_skipper.text: Welcome to the Marina Cafe. Dingle harbour is a long narrow inlet, so the boats are safe in a gale and hard to find in a fog.
The stone tower on the hill above is Eask Tower, built in 1847 as a landmark for ships.
Look out for the Bayrunners. They race the boats for fun, and they win.

then.text: The Race of the Waves has a course, a committee and, as of this year, a trophy. It is nearly a normal event, and I am deeply suspicious.

else.text: Entries in. Tory, Galway, Cork and Dingle are all here, and the only crew missing is Dún Chaoin, who are on the slip, glaring.

then.text: The Dún Chaoin crew say they have rowed these waters since before the Famine, and that the race is theirs by right. Settle it.
The Dún Chaoin crew shake your hand and then, with great dignity, blame the weather. The race is yours, and the Way's. Go and tell Nóra.

else.text: Is this about the race? Nóra is still gathering crews, and a marshal does not blow the whistle on an empty slip.
